title: US-045 — Protect Geocoding Service
excerpt: ## User Story |  | As a JoeKnock system administrator, | I want geocoding requests controlled through the JoeKnock backend, | so that the application does not expose or abuse the external geocoding service. |  | ## Acceptance Criteria |  | - [ ] Frontend does not call geocoding providers directly. | - [ ] MVP geocoding flow is mediated through `POST /api/properties/resolve`. | - [ ] Backend performs reverse geocoding as an internal implementation detail. | - [ ] Requests require authentication. | - [ ] Backend validates coordinates input. | - [ ] Geocoding/provider behavior is handled behind JoeKnock API boundaries. | - [ ] OpenStreetMap attribution requirements are supported by the application. |  | ## Technical Notes |  | - Public geocoding endpoints are not exposed in MVP. | - Geocoding provider calls remain internal to backend property resolution. | - Representatives do not manually edit latitude or longitude. |  | ## Related database tables |  | - properties |  | ## Related API endpoints |  | - POST /api/properties/resolve |  | ## Related ADRs |  | - ADR-012: Organization Data Isolation | - ADR-016: OpenStreetMap Nominatim for MVP Geocoding |  | ## Definition of Done |  | - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. | - [ ] Geocoding access remains backend-mediated and authentication-protected. | - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate.  |

title: US-044 — Handle Network Failure During Interaction
excerpt: ## User Story |  | As a sales representative, | I want my interaction information protected when connectivity is interrupted, | so that I do not lose information while working in the field. |  | ## Acceptance Criteria |  | - [ ] Failed API requests are detected. | - [ ] User receives an understandable error message. | - [ ] Local interaction draft remains available. | - [ ] User can retry submission. | - [ ] Retry behavior does not create duplicate interaction outcomes. | - [ ] Interaction updates use `POST /api/interactions/:id` for revisions. |  | ## Technical Notes |  | - Preserve local draft-first UX for unstable connectivity. | - Retry flows must preserve immutable snapshot rules and existing interaction-group identity. |  | ## Related database tables |  | - properties | - interactions | - users | - statuses |  | ## Related API endpoints |  | - POST /api/properties/:propertyId/interactions | - POST /api/interactions/:id |  | ## Related ADRs |  | - ADR-008: Immutable Interaction Snapshots With Controlled Current-State Flag | - ADR-011: Representative-First Data Capture |  | ## Definition of Done |  | - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. | - [ ] Retry/draft flows do not violate finalized interaction-group and snapshot behavior. | - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate.  |

title: US-043 — Handle API Validation Errors
excerpt: ## User Story |  | As a JoeKnock user,  | I want clear feedback when I submit invalid information,  | so that I can correct mistakes without losing my work. |  | ## Acceptance Criteria |  | - [ ] Required fields are validated.  | - [ ] Invalid data is rejected by the backend.  | - [ ] API returns consistent error responses.  | - [ ] Frontend displays useful validation messages.  | - [ ] Invalid requests do not partially create database records. |  | ## Technical Notes |  | - Derive organization context from the authenticated user or JWT; never trust client-supplied organization identifiers. | - Keep the workflow optimized for in-field, map-first use on tablet-sized screens. | - Cover happy-path, validation, and authorization behavior with focused automated tests. |  | ## Related database tables |  | - organizations | - organization_settings | - users | - teams | - team_users | - properties | - statuses | - interactions |  | ## Related API endpoints |  | - All mutating endpoints |  | ## Related ADRs |  | - ADR-008: Interactions Are Immutable Field Events | - ADR-011: Representative-First Data Capture |  | ## Definition of Done |  | - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. | - [ ] Frontend behavior is validated for the intended field workflow and error states. | - [ ] API behavior matches the documented contract and authorization rules. | - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate for the changed behavior.  |

title: US-042 — Display Interaction Status and Count
excerpt: ## User Story |  | As a sales representative, | I want to see property interaction status and counts on the map, | so that I can quickly understand the area's canvassing history. |  | ## Acceptance Criteria |  | - [ ] Property markers can indicate current relevant status. | - [ ] Interaction count can be displayed where appropriate. | - [ ] Counts follow finalized interaction-group rules for MVP. | - [ ] Snapshot revisions are not shown as additional knocks. | - [ ] Display respects organization isolation and visibility permissions. |  | ## Technical Notes |  | - Map display should use current interaction state data. | - One interaction history exists per organization + property + representative in MVP. |  | ## Related database tables |  | - properties | - interactions | - users | - statuses | - teams |  | ## Related API endpoints |  | - GET /api/map/properties |  | ## Related ADRs |  | - ADR-001: Map-First Application Design | - ADR-008: Immutable Interaction Snapshots With Controlled Current-State Flag | - ADR-009: Current State Is Derived From the Latest Accessible Snapshot |  | ## Definition of Done |  | - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. | - [ ] Map status/count behavior follows finalized reporting and interaction-group semantics. | - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate.  |

title: US-041 — Record Interaction Without Leaving Map
excerpt: ## User Story |  | As a sales representative,  | I want to record an interaction from a map overlay,  | so that I can capture information quickly while standing at the property. |  | ## Acceptance Criteria |  | - [ ] Property remains visible while the interaction form is open.  | - [ ] Interaction form appears as an overlay.  | - [ ] Required fields are kept to a minimum.  | - [ ] User can select a status.  | - [ ] User can enter notes.  | - [ ] User can enter contact information.  | - [ ] User can save the interaction.  | - [ ] Successful save returns the user to the map.  | - [ ] Property marker reflects the updated interaction state. |  | ## Technical Notes |  | - Keep the workflow optimized for in-field, map-first use on tablet-sized screens. | - Honor immutable interaction snapshot rules; revisions create new snapshots instead of overwriting history. |  | ## Related database tables |  | - properties | - interactions | - statuses | - users | - teams | - team_users |  | ## Related API endpoints |  | - POST /api/properties/:propertyId/interactions | - GET /api/map/properties |  | ## Related ADRs |  | - ADR-001: Map-First Application Design | - ADR-008: Interactions Are Immutable Field Events | - ADR-011: Representative-First Data Capture |  | ## Definition of Done |  | - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. | - [ ] Frontend behavior is validated for the intended field workflow and error states. | - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate for the changed behavior.  |

title: US-040 — Select Property from Map
excerpt: ## User Story |  | As a sales representative,  | I want to select a property directly from the map,  | so that I can begin an interaction without navigating through multiple screens. |  | ## Acceptance Criteria |  | - [ ] User can tap/click a property.  | - [ ] Selected property remains visually identifiable.  | - [ ] Property information appears without navigating away from the map.  | - [ ] Interaction controls are accessible from the property overlay.  | - [ ] Map interaction is temporarily controlled while entering interaction information.  | - [ ] User can cancel the interaction and return to the map. |  | ## Technical Notes |  | - Keep the workflow optimized for in-field, map-first use on tablet-sized screens. |  | ## Related database tables |  | - properties | - interactions | - statuses | - users | - teams | - team_users |  | ## Related API endpoints |  | - GET /api/map/properties | - GET /api/properties/:id |  | ## Related ADRs |  | - ADR-001: Map-First Application Design | - ADR-002: Separate Properties From Interactions | - ADR-011: Representative-First Data Capture |  | ## Definition of Done |  | - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. | - [ ] Frontend behavior is validated for the intended field workflow and error states. | - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate for the changed behavior.  |

title: US-039 — View Activity by Representative
excerpt: ## User Story |  | As a manager, | I want to see activity by representative, | so that I can understand team activity. |  | ## Acceptance Criteria |  | - [ ] Report can group interactions by representative. | - [ ] Manager can filter by team. | - [ ] Counts use finalized interaction-group knock rules. | - [ ] Snapshot revisions in an existing interaction group are not counted as additional knocks. | - [ ] Results respect organization isolation and visibility rules. |  | ## Technical Notes |  | - One interaction history exists per organization + property + representative in MVP. | - Reporting must distinguish first interaction creation from later snapshot revisions. |  | ## Related database tables |  | - interactions | - properties | - users | - teams | - statuses |  | ## Related API endpoints |  | - GET /api/reports/activity |  | ## Related ADRs |  | - ADR-008: Immutable Interaction Snapshots With Controlled Current-State Flag | - ADR-009: Current State Is Derived From the Latest Accessible Snapshot | - ADR-012: Organization Data Isolation |  | ## Definition of Done |  | - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. | - [ ] Report output follows finalized representative/group counting rules. | - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate.  |

title: US-038 — View Activity by Status
excerpt: ## User Story |  | As a manager, | I want to see interactions grouped by status, | so that I can understand the results of canvassing activity. |  | ## Acceptance Criteria |  | - [ ] Report can group activity by status. | - [ ] Counts use interaction-group semantics for MVP knock logic. | - [ ] Snapshot revisions in existing interaction groups are not counted as additional knocks. | - [ ] Results respect selected date range. | - [ ] Results respect organization isolation and visibility rules. |  | ## Technical Notes |  | - One interaction history exists per organization + property + representative in MVP. | - Grouping/counting must not imply additional knocks from snapshot edits. |  | ## Related database tables |  | - interactions | - properties | - users | - teams | - statuses |  | ## Related API endpoints |  | - GET /api/reports/activity |  | ## Related ADRs |  | - ADR-008: Immutable Interaction Snapshots With Controlled Current-State Flag | - ADR-009: Current State Is Derived From the Latest Accessible Snapshot | - ADR-012: Organization Data Isolation |  | ## Definition of Done |  | - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. | - [ ] Report output follows finalized interaction-group counting rules. | - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate.  |

title: US-037 — View Activity Report
excerpt: ## User Story |  | As a manager or administrator, | I want to view field activity over a selected date range, | so that I can understand canvassing activity and performance. |  | ## Acceptance Criteria |  | - [ ] Authorized users can request activity data. | - [ ] Report supports date ranges. | - [ ] Report can filter by representative. | - [ ] Report can filter by team. | - [ ] Report can filter by status. | - [ ] Knock counting uses interaction-group semantics. | - [ ] Returning to the same property by the same representative does not create a new knock. | - [ ] Snapshot revisions in an existing interaction group are not counted as additional knocks. | - [ ] Organization isolation and visibility rules are enforced. |  | ## Technical Notes |  | - One interaction history exists per organization + property + representative in MVP. | - `initial_interaction_at` indicates first-knock eligibility for that interaction history. | - Reporting uses interaction/snapshot data; no separate activity-log table is introduced. |  | ## Related database tables |  | - interactions | - properties | - users | - teams | - statuses |  | ## Related API endpoints |  | - GET /api/reports/activity |  | ## Related ADRs |  | - ADR-008: Immutable Interaction Snapshots With Controlled Current-State Flag | - ADR-009: Current State Is Derived From the Latest Accessible Snapshot | - ADR-012: Organization Data Isolation |  | ## Definition of Done |  | - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. | - [ ] Report output follows finalized knock/snapshot counting rules. | - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate.  |

title: US-036 — Enforce Role Permissions
excerpt: ## User Story |  | As a JoeKnock organization,  | I want actions restricted according to user roles,  | so that representatives, managers, and administrators only perform authorized actions. |  | ## Acceptance Criteria |  | ### Representative  |   | Can:  |   | - [ ] View permitted properties.  | - [ ] Create interactions.  | - [ ] View permitted interactions.  | - [ ] Create authorized interaction revisions.  | - [ ] View applicable statuses.  | - [ ] Use map functionality.  | - [ ] Use geocoding functionality.  |   | Cannot:  |   | - [ ] Manage organization users.  | - [ ] Manage teams.  | - [ ] Manage organization settings.  | - [ ] Manage statuses.  |   | ### Manager  |   | Can:  |   | - [ ] Perform representative functions.  | - [ ] View team activity.  | - [ ] Manage teams.  | - [ ] Manage statuses.  | - [ ] View activity reports.  |   | ### Administrator  |   | Can:  |   | - [ ] Perform manager functions.  | - [ ] Manage organization settings.  | - [ ] Manage organization information.  | - [ ] Create users.  | - [ ] Deactivate users.  | - [ ] Manage organization configuration. |  | ## Technical Notes |  | - Derive organization context from the authenticated user or JWT; never trust client-supplied organization identifiers. | - Enforce role permissions and organization isolation for every protected resource lookup. | - Cover happy-path, validation, and authorization behavior with focused automated tests. |  | ## Related database tables |  | - organizations | - organization_settings | - users | - teams | - team_users | - properties | - statuses | - interactions |  | ## Related API endpoints |  | - All protected endpoints | - GET /api/reports/activity | - GET /api/users | - GET /api/teams | - GET /api/statuses |  | ## Related ADRs |  | - ADR-006: Roles Control Access, Not Field Capability | - ADR-012: Organization Data Isolation | - ADR-013: Visibility Controlled Through Organization Settings |  | ## Definition of Done |  | - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. | - [ ] API behavior matches the documented contract and authorization rules. | - [ ] Organization isolation and role permissions are verified for the affected paths. | - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate for the changed behavior.  |

title: US-035 — Enforce Organization Isolation
excerpt: ## User Story |  | As a JoeKnock organization,  | I want my data isolated from other organizations,  | so that another organization cannot access our properties, users, or interactions. |  | ## Acceptance Criteria |  | - [ ] Every authenticated request has an organization context.  | - [ ] Property access verifies organization ownership.  | - [ ] Interaction access verifies organization ownership.  | - [ ] User access verifies organization ownership.  | - [ ] Team access verifies organization ownership.  | - [ ] Status access verifies organization ownership.  | - [ ] Organization settings cannot be accessed by another organization.  | - [ ] Changing a resource ID in a request cannot bypass organization isolation.  | - [ ] Cross-organization access attempts return an appropriate authorization/not-found response. |  | ## Technical Notes |  | - Derive organization context from the authenticated user or JWT; never trust client-supplied organization identifiers. | - Enforce role permissions and organization isolation for every protected resource lookup. | - Use the documented MVP schema and preserve historical references instead of hard-deleting records. | - Cover happy-path, validation, and authorization behavior with focused automated tests. |  | ## Related database tables |  | - organizations | - organization_settings | - users | - teams | - team_users | - properties | - statuses | - interactions |  | ## Related API endpoints |  | - All protected endpoints |  | ## Related ADRs |  | - ADR-004: PostgreSQL Relational Database | - ADR-006: Roles Control Access, Not Field Capability | - ADR-012: Organization Data Isolation | - ADR-013: Visibility Controlled Through Organization Settings |  | ## Definition of Done |  | - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. | - [ ] API behavior matches the documented contract and authorization rules. | - [ ] Persistence changes align with the documented MVP schema and preserve historical integrity. | - [ ] Organization isolation and role permissions are verified for the affected paths. | - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate for the changed behavior.  |

title: US-034 — Restrict Representative Visibility
excerpt: ## User Story |  | As an organization administrator,  | I want to configure what representatives can see,  | so that field information is shared according to our organization's workflow. |  | ## Acceptance Criteria |  | Organization can configure:  |   | ```text  | own  | team  | organization  | ```  |   | For `own`:  |   | - [ ] Representative sees their own interactions.  |   | For `team`:  |   | - [ ] Representative sees interactions associated with their team visibility.  |   | For `organization`:  |   | - [ ] Representative can see organization-wide interactions.  |   | Managers and administrators retain their appropriate elevated visibility. |  | ## Technical Notes |  | - Derive organization context from the authenticated user or JWT; never trust client-supplied organization identifiers. | - Enforce role permissions and organization isolation for every protected resource lookup. |  | ## Related database tables |  | - organization_settings | - users | - teams | - team_users | - properties | - interactions | - statuses |  | ## Related API endpoints |  | - GET /api/organization/settings | - PATCH /api/organization/settings | - GET /api/properties | - GET /api/map/properties |  | ## Related ADRs |  | - ADR-006: Roles Control Access, Not Field Capability | - ADR-008: Interactions Are Immutable Field Events | - ADR-012: Organization Data Isolation | - ADR-013: Visibility Controlled Through Organization Settings |  | ## Definition of Done |  | - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. | - [ ] API behavior matches the documented contract and authorization rules. | - [ ] Organization isolation and role permissions are verified for the affected paths. | - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate for the changed behavior.  |

title: US-032 — View Interaction Snapshot
excerpt: ## User Story |  | As a user with permission to view an interaction,  | I want to view the details of a specific interaction snapshot,  | so that I can understand what information was recorded. |  | ## Acceptance Criteria |  | - [ ] Snapshot can be retrieved by ID.  | - [ ] Snapshot displays status.  | - [ ] Snapshot displays interaction date.  | - [ ] Snapshot displays notes when present.  | - [ ] Snapshot displays contact information when present.  | - [ ] Snapshot identifies the representative who recorded it.  | - [ ] Snapshot identifies the associated property. |  | ## Technical Notes |  | - Derive organization context from the authenticated user or JWT; never trust client-supplied organization identifiers. | - Keep the workflow optimized for in-field, map-first use on tablet-sized screens. | - Honor immutable interaction snapshot rules; revisions create new snapshots instead of overwriting history. |  | ## Related database tables |  | - interactions | - properties | - users | - statuses |  | ## Related API endpoints |  | - GET /api/interactions/:id |  | ## Related ADRs |  | - ADR-008: Interactions Are Immutable Field Events | - ADR-010: Historical Status Information Is Preserved | - ADR-011: Representative-First Data Capture |  | ## Definition of Done |  | - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. | - [ ] Frontend behavior is validated for the intended field workflow and error states. | - [ ] API behavior matches the documented contract and authorization rules. | - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate for the changed behavior.  |

title: US-031 — Update Interaction
excerpt: ## User Story |  | As a sales representative, | I want to update an interaction when information changes, | so that the current record reflects the latest information while preserving the original history. |  | ## Acceptance Criteria |  | - [ ] User can edit an authorized interaction. | - [ ] Interaction updates use `POST /api/interactions/:id`. | - [ ] Existing snapshot field values are not overwritten. | - [ ] New immutable snapshot is created. | - [ ] New snapshot keeps the same `interaction_group_id`. | - [ ] `initial_interaction_at` remains unchanged. | - [ ] `changed_at` is updated on the new snapshot. | - [ ] Previous snapshot is preserved and no interaction deletion occurs. | - [ ] Existing notes are copied to the new snapshot unless changed by the representative. |  | ## Technical Notes |  | - One interaction history exists per organization + property + representative in MVP. | - Returning to the same property updates existing interaction history rather than creating a new one. | - Only owner representatives edit their interaction records; managers/admins are view-only on others. |  | ## Related database tables |  | - interactions | - properties | - users | - statuses |  | ## Related API endpoints |  | - POST /api/interactions/:id |  | ## Related ADRs |  | - ADR-008: Immutable Interaction Snapshots With Controlled Current-State Flag | - ADR-012: Organization Data Isolation |  | ## Definition of Done |  | - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. | - [ ] API behavior matches documented ownership and immutability rules. | - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate.  |

title: US-030 — Save Interaction Draft
excerpt: ## User Story |  | As a sales representative,  | I want my partially completed interaction to be protected from accidental data loss,  | so that a dead battery, dropped connection, or accidental interruption does not force me to start over. |  | ## Acceptance Criteria |  | - [ ] Interaction form can save a local draft.  | - [ ] Draft is stored locally on the device.  | - [ ] Draft can be restored after the form is reopened.  | - [ ] Draft does not create a database interaction until the user saves/submits it.  | - [ ] Draft can be discarded intentionally.  | - [ ] Draft data is associated with the appropriate property. |  | ## Technical Notes |  | - Keep the workflow optimized for in-field, map-first use on tablet-sized screens. | - Draft preservation and retry behavior must avoid creating duplicate persisted interactions after interrupted submissions. |  | ## Related database tables |  | - None until submission; local draft storage should be keyed to the selected property context |  | ## Related API endpoints |  | - None; this story is local-client behavior until data is submitted. |  | ## Related ADRs |  | - ADR-008: Interactions Are Immutable Field Events | - ADR-011: Representative-First Data Capture |  | ## Definition of Done |  | - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. | - [ ] Frontend behavior is validated for the intended field workflow and error states. | - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate for the changed behavior.  |

revisions create new snapshots instead of overwriting history. |  | ## Related database tables |  | - properties |  | ## Related API endpoints |  | - POST /api/properties/:propertyId/interactions |  | ## Related ADRs |  | - ADR-004: PostgreSQL Relational Database | - ADR-008: Interactions Are Immutable Field Events | - ADR-011: Representative-First Data Capture |  | ## Definition of Done |  | - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. | - [ ] Frontend behavior is validated for the intended field workflow and error states. | - [ ] API behavior matches the documented contract and authorization rules. | - [ ] Persistence changes align with the documented MVP schema and preserve historical integrity. | - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate for the changed behavior.  |

title: US-028 — View Property Interactions (Current State)
excerpt: ## User Story |  | As a sales representative, | I want to see the current interaction state for a property, | so that I know the latest authorized information before recording updates. |  | ## Acceptance Criteria |  | - [ ] Property interaction endpoint returns current snapshots by default. | - [ ] Multiple interaction groups can exist at one property across representatives. | - [ ] Current snapshots are identifiable. | - [ ] Results respect organization isolation and visibility permissions. | - [ ] Normal user-facing historical snapshot timeline is not exposed in MVP. |  | ## Technical Notes |  | - This story is current-state focused to avoid overlap with deferred user-facing history work. | - Historical snapshots remain preserved internally for reporting/support use. |  | ## Related database tables |  | - properties | - interactions | - users | - statuses |  | ## Related API endpoints |  | - GET /api/properties/:propertyId/interactions |  | ## Related ADRs |  | - ADR-002: Separate Properties From Interactions | - ADR-008: Immutable Interaction Snapshots With Controlled Current-State Flag | - ADR-015: Historical Interaction Data Is Preserved but Not User-Facing in MVP |  | ## Definition of Done |  | - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. | - [ ] API behavior matches documented current-state semantics. | - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate.  |

title: US-027 — View Property
excerpt: ## User Story |  | As a sales representative, | I want to view property information after selecting it on the map, | so that I can review its current information before recording an interaction. |  | ## Acceptance Criteria |  | - [ ] Selecting a property retrieves property details. | - [ ] Address information is displayed. | - [ ] Current interaction state for that property is retrievable for authorized users. | - [ ] User can access interaction workflow from the property view. | - [ ] Property and interaction data respect organization/visibility permissions. |  | ## Technical Notes |  | - Property details and current interaction state may require both property and property-interactions endpoints. | - MVP UI uses current state and does not expose a normal user-facing historical timeline. |  | ## Related database tables |  | - properties | - interactions | - users | - statuses |  | ## Related API endpoints |  | - GET /api/properties/:id | - GET /api/properties/:propertyId/interactions |  | ## Related ADRs |  | - ADR-001: Map-First Application Design | - ADR-002: Separate Properties From Interactions | - ADR-015: Historical Interaction Data Is Preserved but Not User-Facing in MVP |  | ## Definition of Done |  | - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. | - [ ] API behavior matches documented authorization and visibility rules. | - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate.  |

title: US-026 — Create Property
excerpt: ## User Story |  | As a sales representative, | I want JoeKnock to create a property when I encounter a location that is not already in the system, | so that I can record an interaction at that property. |  | ## Acceptance Criteria |  | - [ ] Property resolution starts with `POST /api/properties/resolve` using representative-selected coordinates. | - [ ] Backend reverse geocodes coordinates and normalizes address for matching. | - [ ] Existing property is returned when found for the authenticated organization. | - [ ] New property is created when no organization-scoped match exists. | - [ ] Created/returned property is organization-owned based on authentication context. | - [ ] Property creation does not require client-supplied organization identifiers. | - [ ] Representatives do not manually edit latitude or longitude in MVP. |  | ## Technical Notes |  | - This story focuses on persistence/ownership outcomes of property resolution. | - Property identity is backend-controlled and organization-scoped. | - Geocoding remains internal; frontend interacts only with JoeKnock API. |  | ## Related database tables |  | - properties |  | ## Related API endpoints |  | - POST /api/properties/resolve |  | ## Related ADRs |  | - ADR-002: Separate Properties From Interactions | - ADR-012: Organization Data Isolation | - ADR-016: OpenStreetMap Nominatim for MVP Geocoding |  | ## Definition of Done |  | - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. | - [ ] API behavior matches the documented contract and authorization rules. | - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate for the changed behavior.  |

title: US-023 — Identify Property from Map Location
excerpt: ## User Story |  | As a sales representative, | I want to select a location on the map and identify its address, | so that I can record an interaction without manually entering the property address. |  | ## Acceptance Criteria |  | - [ ] User can select a location/property on the map. | - [ ] Frontend sends selected coordinates to `POST /api/properties/resolve`. | - [ ] Backend performs reverse geocoding as an internal implementation detail. | - [ ] Backend receives the geocoded address and normalizes it for matching. | - [ ] Backend checks for an existing property within the authenticated organization. | - [ ] Existing property is returned when found. | - [ ] New property is created and returned when no match exists. | - [ ] Frontend does not call the geocoding provider directly. | - [ ] Geocoding/provider errors are handled gracefully. |  | ## Technical Notes |  | - Use the finalized MVP property-resolution flow: coordinates -> reverse geocoding -> normalized address -> organization-scoped lookup/create -> resolved property. | - The geocoder-returned address is the address JoeKnock uses in MVP. | - Representatives do not manually edit latitude or longitude. | - Preserve organization isolation for all property resolution behavior. |  | ## Related database tables |  | - properties |  | ## Related API endpoints |  | - POST /api/properties/resolve |  | ## Related ADRs |  | - ADR-001: Map-First Application Design | - ADR-002: Separate Properties From Interactions | - ADR-012: Organization Data Isolation | - ADR-016: OpenStreetMap Nominatim for MVP Geocoding |  | ## Definition of Done |  | - [ ] Acceptance criteria are implemented and verified. | - [ ] API behavior matches the documented contract and authorization rules. | - [ ] Automated tests are added or updated where appropriate for the changed behavior.  |
